summary: Erik J. Hammerstrom specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned his PhD from Indiana University Bloomington (attested 2010) and served as assistant professor of religion at Pacific Lutheran University (attested 2016).

Erik Pema Kunsang is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who taught Douglas S. Duckworth and Cortland Dahl. He served as director of Rangjung Yeshe Publications around 1981 and as resident teacher at Rangjung Yeshe Gomde Denmark.

Erik Zürcher worked in Sinology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Leiden University (PhD ca. 1947–1959) and under Paul Demiéville, Jan Julius Lodewijk Duyvendak, Édouard Chavannes, and Prabodh Chandra Bagchi. He served as director at Leiden (1961–1993).

Erik-Jan Zürcher is a historian and linguist who completed his BA and PhD at Leiden University. He held posts at Radboud University Nijmegen (1977–1997), Leiden University (professor from 1997), and the International Institute of Social History (director, 2008–2012).

Sinologist Erling von Mende studied at the universities of Hamburg, Freiburg, Bonn, and Cologne, where he completed his PhD (1969) and habilitation (by 1979). He served as professor of Sinology at the Free University of Berlin from 1983 to 2007.
Ernest Arthur Gardner was an archaeologist and historian who studied at Gonville and Caius College around 1880–1884. He later held a post at the University of London from 1924 to 1926.

Ernest Bender worked in Indology and linguistics, studying at Temple University and the University of Pennsylvania under W. Norman Brown, Zellig Harris, and Henry Hoenigswald. He was a professor at Pennsylvania (1950–1989) and edited the Journal of the American Oriental Society (1964–1988).

Ernest Fenollosa worked in philosophy, Japanology, and art history, studying at Harvard and the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston. He held posts at the University of Tokyo (from 1878) and the Museum of Fine Arts, Boston (1890–1896).

Ernest John Henry Mackay was an archaeologist and Indologist who earned his BA, MA, and DLitt at the University of Bristol. He served as Custodian of Antiquities in Mandatory Palestine (1919–1922) and Special Officer for Exploration with the Archaeological Survey of India (ca. 1926–1932).

Ernest Renan worked in religious studies, history, and linguistics, studying at Saint-Sulpice, Collège de France, and under Eugène Burnouf and Étienne Marc Quatremère. He served at the Bibliothèque nationale de France (1851–1860) and as professor at the Collège de France from 1861.

Philosopher Ernest Sosa studied at the University of Miami and the University of Pittsburgh under Roderick M. Chisholm. He was a professor at Brown University from 1964 and Board of Governors Professor of Philosophy at Rutgers University (1998–2006).

Historian and archaeologist Ernst Curtius studied under Friedrich Gottlieb Welcker and Christian August Brandis at Bonn and Göttingen. He held professorships at the Humboldt University of Berlin (from 1844) and Göttingen (1855–1867), and directed the Altes Museum (ca. 1872–1896).

Linguist and historian Ernst Förstemann studied at Berlin and Halle under Karl Lachmann, Franz Bopp, and August Friedrich Pott. He served as librarian at the Fürst zu Stolberg-Wernigerodesche Bibliothek (from 1851) and director of the Saxon State Library Dresden (1865–1887).

Ernst Fürlinger is a scholar of religious studies and Indology who completed his habilitation at the University of Vienna. He taught at Vienna (2006–2016) and held research and leadership positions at the University for Continuing Education Krems beginning in 2007.

Ernst Gombrich studied at the University of Vienna. An art historian, he held posts at the University of London (1956–1959) and the Warburg Institute, where he was a research assistant (from 1936) and director (1959–1976).

Indologist Ernst Haas studied at Bonn, Tübingen, and Berlin, working under Albrecht Weber. He held posts at the British Museum from 1866 and served as professor of Sanskrit at University College London from 1875.
Ernst Haeckel studied at Frederick William University / Humboldt University of Berlin around 1854–1857. He held a post at the University of Jena from approximately 1862 to 1909.

Ernst Johann Eitel worked in Sinology and Buddhist studies. After earning his MA and PhD at the University of Tübingen, he served as professor and lecturer of German language and literature at the University of Adelaide from around 1897 to 1908.

Ernst Kuhn worked in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian/Central Asian studies, studying under Albrecht Weber and Rudolf von Roth at Berlin, Tübingen, and Halle. He was later a professor at Heidelberg (from 1875) and Munich (1877–1917).

Ernst Leumann worked in Indology, Iranian/Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied under Albrecht Weber and earned doctorates at Leipzig and Strasbourg. He worked on a Sanskrit dictionary at Oxford and became professor and rector at Strasbourg (1884–1910).
